title: Snap a Textbook Page, Get the Homework Explained | vitalii.no
description:
When a child needed help with a specific printed page from a school textbook, there was no way to look it up digitally. Someone had to find the physical book, flip to the right page, and work out what the task actually was by hand — every single time, even for pages that had already been explained before.

A new ingestion script turns a scanned PDF or a folder of photos into page images that stay only on the home PC, never uploaded anywhere public. A lookup script takes one printed page for one specific child, hands an AI agent that page plus the surrounding pages for context, and lets it read the page exactly once. The subject, a short context summary, and the actual list of tasks get stored in a database keyed by child, book, and page number.

If the same page comes up again — for the same child or another one — the system reuses the stored answer instead of reading it a second time. A printed page gets looked up once and turned into an explained list of tasks, cutting repeated work down to pages nobody has seen yet.
